propositions.text: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is a Mexican citizen; spouse is Guatemalan; children are US citizens.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is a citizen of Mexico. Her spouse, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of Guatemala. Their children, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, andXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX are citizens of the United States (US).

propositions.text: Despite sympathy, the appeal is dismissed for reasons that follow.
propositions.quote: Although I have a great deal of sympathy for XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family, I dismiss this appeal for the reasons that follow.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the family members' citizenships and dismisses the appeal despite sympathy.

propositions.text: The case arises from US Trump administration policy changes affecting the family.
propositions.quote: The circumstances of this case are particularly unfortunate and arise due to certain policy changes brought in by the Trump administration in the US.

propositions.text: The family entered the US illegally as children but tried to live productive lives.
propositions.quote: They crossed into the US by illegal means but did everything they could to study, work and have a productive life in the US.

propositions.text: Before 2008, they were told they were ineligible to regularize status; in 2012 they became eligible for DACA.
propositions.quote: Prior to 2008, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX consulted a lawyer who told her that she and her spouse were not eligible for any programme that would allow them to regularize their status in the US. Finally, in 2012, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her spouse became eligible to enroll in the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) programme.

propositions.text: In 2018, renewal of DACA was not responded to; husband lost work permit and was fired.
propositions.quote: In the fall of 2018, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX applied to renew his DACA status but he never received a response to his application. In XXXX 2018, he was fired from his work because his permit had expired and there was no sign that it would be renewed by the Trump administration.

propositions.text: The family came to Canada to claim refugee status fearing harm to children if deported to origin countries.
propositions.quote: At this point, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family made their way to Canada to claim refugee status. They fear that, if they are deported from the US to their countries of origin, their children will suffer serious harm as orphans in the child welfare system in the US.

paragraphs.summary: The court describes the family's US entry, DACA status, loss of work permit, and refugee claim in Canada fearing harm to children.

propositions.text: RPD found the parents credible about events described.
propositions.quote: The RPD found XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXandXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX to be very credible as to the events they described.

propositions.text: RPD found the key issue was forward-looking risk in countries of origin.
propositions.quote: the determinative issue in the case was the issue of whether XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family faced a forward-looking risk in their respective countries of origin.

propositions.text: RPD found violence and poverty feared in Mexico and Guatemala is generalized risk not differing from others.
propositions.quote: the violence and poverty that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX fear in Mexico and Guatemala is a generalized risk of the kind that does not differ from the risk face by others in or from those countries.

propositions.text: RPD found children's risk of separation and foster care does not amount to persecution or serious harm under IRPA.
propositions.quote: the risk they faced of being separated from their parents and living in foster homes did not amount to persecution on a Convention ground within the meaning of s. 96 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) or one of the forms of serious harm that would make them persons in need of protection within s. 97 of the IRPA.

propositions.text: RPD found IRPA sections 96 and 97 do not include family unity notion; family separation alone insufficient for asylum claim.
propositions.quote: sections 96 and 97 of the IRPA do not include the notion of family unity and that it is established in the case law that the separation of families, in itself, is not enough to found an asylum claim.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found parents credible but risks in origin countries generalized; children's separation not persecution under IRPA; family unity not asylum ground.

propositions.text: Appellants do not contest RPD's conclusion on parents' refugee or protection status in Mexico and Guatemala.
propositions.quote: The Appellants make no arguments to contest the RPD's conclusion that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXandXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection in relation to Mexico and Guatemala respectively.

propositions.text: Appellants focus arguments on children's situation in the US, alleging RPD erred in finding children not persons in need of protection there.
propositions.quote: Instead, they focus their arguments on the situation of the children in the US. They argue that the RPD erred in finding that the children are not persons in need of protection in the US.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants accept RPD's findings on parents but argue RPD erred on children's protection status in the US.

propositions.text: Court's role is to review all evidence and decide if RPD decision was correct.
propositions.quote: My role is to look at all the evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.

propositions.text: Court agrees with RPD that parents were credible.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXand XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX were very credible.

propositions.text: Court finds RPD correct that family are neither Convention Refugees nor persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: However, the RPD was correct in finding that the XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family are neither Convention Refugees nor persons in need of protection.

propositions.text: Evidence insufficient to establish children would face serious harm amounting to need for protection if returned to US.
propositions.quote: I find that the evidence in this case is insufficient to establish that, if they return to the US, the children would be subjected to any of the forms of serious harm that would make them persons in need of protection as that term is defined in s. 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with RPD on parents' credibility and protection status, and finds insufficient evidence for children's protection claim in US.

propositions.text: Parents did not contest RPD's finding that forward-looking risk in Mexico or Guatemala does not meet protection criteria.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXandXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX did not make any arguments to contest the RPD's finding that the forward-looking risk they would face if they return to either Mexico or Guatemala is not the kind of risk that would make them persons in need of protection under s. 97 of the IRPA.

propositions.text: Court reviewed all evidence including audio recording.
propositions.quote: Nevertheless, I have conducted a review of all of the evidence in this case, including the audio-recording.

propositions.text: Court finds RPD correct that general violence and insecurity in Mexico and Guatemala do not make parents persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: Based on this review, I find that the RPD was correct in its conclusion that the general violence, criminality, and insecurity to which XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX might be subject in Mexico or Guatemala do not make them persons in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court confirms RPD's finding that parents face generalized risks in Mexico and Guatemala not warranting protection.

propositions.text: To claim protection for risk to life or cruel treatment, claimant must show risk is personal and not general to others from that country.
propositions.quote: When a person alleges that they are a person in need of protection due to a risk to their life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, they must not only establish that they likely would face such a risk personally in their country. They must also show that this risk is not faced generally by other individuals in or from that country.

propositions.text: If claimant's risk is same as general risk faced by others, they will not be persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: If the personal risk faced by the claimant is the same risk faced generally by others in or from their country of origin, they will not be found to be persons in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the legal test that personal risk must exceed general country risk to qualify for protection.

propositions.text: Parents' reluctance to return to countries with which they have little connection is understandable.
propositions.quote: it is understandable that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX are reluctant to return to countries to which they have almost no connection due to the fact that they left when they were very young.

propositions.text: Parents' concern about violence and insecurity in Mexico and Guatemala is understandable.
propositions.quote: It is also understandable that they may be concerned about the general level of violence, criminality, and insecurity in Mexico and Guatemala.

propositions.text: Risk faced by parents in Mexico or Guatemala does not differ significantly from that faced by others from those countries.
propositions.quote: the risk they would face in returning to either of these countries does not differ significantly from the risk faced by others in and from those countries.

propositions.text: RPD was correct to find parents are not persons in need of protection in relation to Mexico and Guatemala.
propositions.quote: Therefore, the RPD was correct to find that they are not persons in need of protection in relation to those countries.

propositions.text: Parents did not allege and evidence does not support Convention refugee claim in relation to Mexico and Guatemala.
propositions.quote: In addition, they did not allege, and the evidence does not support, any claim that they would be Convention refugees in relation to those countries.

propositions.text: Despite difficult situation caused by US policy changes, RPD was correct to deny asylum claims of parents.
propositions.quote: Therefore, despite the untenable situation that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX have been placed in due to changes in US policy, the RPD was correct to deny the asylum claims filed by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds parents' fears understandable but agrees with RPD that risks are generalized and asylum claims rightly denied.

propositions.text: Appellants argue RPD erred in finding children not persons in need of protection in the US.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family argue that the RPD erred in finding that the children were not persons in need of protection in relation to the United States.

propositions.text: Court is open to argument that separation of children from parents may be cruel and unusual punishment in some cases.
propositions.quote: I am open to the argument that the separation of children from their parents may amount to cruel and unusual punishment in some circumstances,

propositions.text: Such argument requires sufficient evidence, which is lacking here.
propositions.quote: However, this argument needs to be supported by sufficient evidence which is lacking in this case.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue RPD erred on children's protection; court is open to argument but finds evidence lacking.

propositions.text: Family argues children will suffer cruel and unusual treatment if forced to return to US due to likely deportation of parents.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family argue that their children will suffer cruel and unusual treatment or punishment if they are forced to return to the US. According to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX will likely be deported if they and their family return to the US.

propositions.text: They argue US cannot protect minor claimants and rising enforcement harms children's development.
propositions.quote: They argue that the US cannot protect minor claimants and that rising immigration enforcement in the US causes long-lasting harmful effects on a child's developmental well-being.

paragraphs.summary: The family argues children face cruel treatment in US due to likely parental deportation and poor protection.

propositions.text: Court disagrees that family separation alone can found asylum claim.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family that the RPD erred in finding that family separation cannot, in itself, found a claim for asylum.

propositions.text: Family objects that RPD cited only one decision supporting family separation principle.
propositions.quote: They take issue with the fact that the RPD cited only one decision in support of this principle.

propositions.text: The cited decision is a RAD decision recognized by Immigration and Refugee Board and relies on Federal Court case law.
propositions.quote: I note that the decision cited by the RPD is a RAD decision that was identified as a decision of interest by the Immigration and Refugee Board. The decision relies on Federal Court case law that has made this precise finding.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects family's objection about limited case citation and upholds principle that family separation alone is insufficient for asylum.

propositions.text: Court disagrees that family unity principle in Convention on Rights of Child means asylum claim can be based solely on family unity or best interests of child.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family that the fact that the principle of family unity is contained in the Convention on the Rights of the Child means that a claim for asylum can simply be based on the principle of family unity or the best interests of the child.

propositions.text: Family relies on humanitarian and compassionate application cases to support their argument.
propositions.quote: I note that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family seek to rely on court decisions dealing with humanitarian and compassionate applications to make their argument.

propositions.text: Federal Court in Kim case held best interests of child applied differently in asylum claims versus humanitarian and compassionate grounds.
propositions.quote: However, the Federal Court in the Kim case, cited by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family, specifically addressed this issue.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects family's reliance on family unity and best interests of child for asylum, citing Kim case distinction.

propositions.text: Kim case explains refugee definition under section 96 is strict; best interests of child considered procedurally but cannot override definition.
propositions.quote: The Canadian immigration system provides for several methods by which to gain entry into Canada, one of which is to be a refugee under section 96. Section 96 provides a strict definition that is either met or not by the claimant in question. If the definition is met, then the claimant may be able to enter Canada as a refugee. If, on the other hand, the definition is not met, then the claimant may not enter Canada pursuant to that section and other options become available to him or her. One remaining option is pursuant to section 25, wherein the Minister at his discretion may grant an exemption "from any applicable criteria or obligation of" the IRPA. It is under section 25 that a substantive and thorough analysis of the best interests of the child is performed. At the stage of a section 96 application, it is sufficient that the best interests of the child are taken into account procedurally, as directed by the Guidelines [relating to child refugee claimants]. The Court must reiterate that the best interests of the child cannot shoehorn a refugee claimant into the section 96 definition if the child's claim would otherwise be rejected, but it can influence the process which leads to that decision.

paragraphs.summary: The Kim case clarifies that best interests of child influence process but cannot expand strict refugee definition under section 96.

propositions.text: Kim case found Convention on Rights of Child and Guidelines add nuances recognizing children's distinct rights in refugee claims.
propositions.quote: In Kim, the Court found that the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Guidelines relating to child claimants add nuances to the determination of whether a child fits the definition of a refugee under section 96 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

propositions.text: Children can be persecuted or harmed in ways not amounting to persecution or serious harm for adults.
propositions.quote: These nuances are based on an appreciation that children have distinct rights that are in need of special protection, and can be persecuted or harmed in ways that would not amount to persecution or serious harm for an adult.

propositions.text: Decision-makers must consider rights in Convention on Rights of Child to determine well-founded fear of persecution for child claimants.
propositions.quote: The Court found in Kim that, when determining whether a child claiming refugee claimant fits the definition in section 96 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, decision-makers must inform themselves of the rights recognized in the Convention on the Rights of the Child. It is the denial of these rights which may determine whether or not a child has a well-founded fear of persecution if returned to his or her country of origin.

paragraphs.summary: Kim case requires considering children's distinct rights under Convention on Rights of Child in refugee determinations.

propositions.text: Same analysis applies to children as persons in need of protection under section 97 IRPA.
propositions.quote: In my view, the same analysis applies to assessments of whether children are persons in need of protection under s. 97 Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

paragraphs.summary: The court applies Kim analysis to children under section 97 protection claims.

propositions.text: Family filed National Documentation Package section about US practice of separating children from parents crossing border illegally.
propositions.quote: The only documentary evidence that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family have filed in support of their argument that the children likely would be subjected to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment in the US is a section of the National Documentation Package for the US which discusses the country's practice of separating children from their parents when they were apprehended for crossing the border illegally.

propositions.text: This document is not relevant to children born in US who are US citizens.
propositions.quote: However, this is not the situation faced by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX children who were born in the US and who are all US citizens. Therefore, I find that this document has little relevance to the situation likely faced by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX children if they return to the US.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the family's documentary evidence about border separations irrelevant to their US-born citizen children.

propositions.text: Mother testified children traumatized by husband's possible deportation and possible separation at Canadian border.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX testified that her children were traumatized by the idea of her husband being deported from the US. They were also traumatized when they thought they might be separated from their parents at the Canadian border.

propositions.text: This is the extent of evidence supporting argument that separation would be cruel and unusual treatment.
propositions.quote: However, that is the extent of the evidence that was before the RPD, and that is before me, to support the argument made by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family that her children's separation from their parents would amount to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the mother's testimony of children's trauma but finds no further evidence supporting cruel treatment claim.

propositions.text: Family argues separation causes psychological, behavioural, cognitive effects on children.
propositions.quote: Although XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family argue that separating children from their families has a range of psychological, behavioural and cognitive effects,

propositions.text: No social science or psychological evidence was before RPD or RAD to support this argument.
propositions.quote: there was no social science or psychological evidence before the RPD or now before the RAD to support this argument.

propositions.text: Amnesty International argued forced separation at US border amounted to ill-treatment and torture in some cases.
propositions.quote: It is true, as noted by XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family, that Amnesty International has argued that the forcible separation of children from their family members at the US southern border has in some cases amounted to ill-treatment and torture.

propositions.text: Amnesty referred to forced separation at border, not situation of US-born citizen children here.
propositions.quote: However, the organization was referring to the forced separation of children from their parents as they crossed the border, where in some cases, according to the organization, children were held in cages, locked up in freezing cells without adequate food or medicine. That is not the situation for XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX children who are US citizens born in the US.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no supporting evidence for psychological harm claims and distinguishes Amnesty's border separation cases from this family's situation.

propositions.text: Evidence insufficient to find children's separation effects amount to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.
propositions.quote: Overall, the evidence in this case is not sufficient to enable me to find that the effects on XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX children if they end up being separated from their parents is of such a degree, as to amount to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.

propositions.text: Parents have family members in US who are citizens or permanent residents.
propositions.quote: This is especially the case, since XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX do have family members who are citizens or permanent residents of the US. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX has a brother who is a citizen of the US and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX has a sister who she testified was a permanent resident of the US.

propositions.text: Mother testified children could possibly live with uncle in US but support and foster care issues exist.
propositions.quote: When the RPD asked XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX if it would be possible for the children to live with her or her husband's family members in the US, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX replied that it would be difficult. When the RPD asked whether it would nevertheless be possible, she said it would probably be possible but it would depend on the system. Later, in answer to her counsel's questions, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX said that, in order for her children to stay with their uncle in the US, she and her husband would have to be able to support them based on their earnings in Mexico or Guatemala or else they would be placed in the foster-care system.

propositions.text: Court agrees separation would have significant effects but evidence insufficient to establish cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.
propositions.quote: I completely agree with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family that their separation from their children will have significant effects on them. However, I do not find that the evidence in this case is sufficient to establish that the effects on the children would amount to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds evidence insufficient to establish cruel treatment from separation, noting family support possibilities and acknowledging significant effects.

propositions.text: Family argues discrimination against children as Latinos in US amounts to persecution.
propositions.quote: I also do not agree with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and her family that any discrimination that the children may face in the US due to their being Latino amounts to persecution.

propositions.text: Not all discrimination amounts to persecution; persecution requires serious, repeated discrimination with prejudicial consequences.
propositions.quote: While all discrimination is unacceptable, not all discrimination amounts to persecution. In order for discrimination against a person to amount to persecution, it must be serious and occur with repetition. It must also have consequences of a prejudicial nature for the person, such as when an individual is denied a core human right, such as the right to practice religion or to earn a livelihood.

propositions.text: Children were harassed and bullied in school.
propositions.quote: In this case, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX testified that other children would harass and bully his children in school.

propositions.text: Such harassment is unacceptable but not widespread or significant enough to be persecution.
propositions.quote: In my view, such discriminatory actions, although unacceptable, are not sufficiently widespread or significant to rise to the level of persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects family's claim that discrimination against children is persecution, finding harassment insufficiently serious or widespread.

propositions.text: The RPD did not err in concluding the children do not face serious persecution or serious harm in the US
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD did not err in concluding that the children do not face a serious possibility of persecution or the likelihood of any of the kinds of serious harm that would make them persons in need of protection in the US.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD did not err in concluding the children do not face serious persecution or harm in the US.

propositions.text: Dismiss the appeal and confirm the RPD decision that the appellants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection
propositions.quote: I must dismiss the appeal and confirm the decision of the RPD that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXandXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD decision that the appellants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.

propositions.text: Echo the RPD's view that claims may raise humanitarian and compassionate issues for a different entity and process beyond RPD and RAD jurisdiction
propositions.quote: I echo the RPD's view that, even though these claims do not qualify under the asylum provisions of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, they may raise humanitarian and compassionate issues to be decided by a different entity through a different application process over which the RPD and the RAD have no jurisdiction.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the RPD that the claims may raise humanitarian issues for another entity beyond RPD and RAD jurisdiction.
